correctness.rationale: The exponentially killed Brownian endpoint has a bilateral exponential density. Its exact two jump-tail series give drift = mean reward/mean renewal time; all increments have integrable moments. The strictly decreasing log derivative and endpoint signs prove existence and uniqueness for all allowed rates. Hyperbolic convexity is the critical global inequality. Implicit derivatives are rigorously signed. Near-perfect and large-latency scaling are proved by localized root balances with exponentially small residual terms. A standalone executed checker independently reproduced 116 numerical assertions; finite samples are not proof.

value.rationale: The physically motivated reset-frequency optimization has a complete all-parameter uniqueness result. Deterministic immobilization delays shift the optimum strictly and change the singular near-perfect asymmetry exponent from 2 to 2/3 in the optimal reset rate. This quantitatively distinguishes whether return overhead is negligible in a genuine asymmetric local-capture motor, beyond reporting the already known current expression or a routine finite table. Does not claim finite-potential transport or general efficiency optimization.
